messages:
Nina: Pushing a different idea for the first-run surface: small modal overlay that walks through a 3-step setup (API key, sample project, quick test) vs the persistent rail. Want quick reactions on pros/cons. Fig link: https://figma.redwood/onboard-modal-v1
Ravi: Modal is focused, which is good for new users but could be annoying for returning ones. We need a remember-me toggle and a clear escape (close + skip). Also check that modal doesn't block screenreader navigation to skip link.
Olivia: From UX: modal allows step-by-step hand-holding, good for retention. But performance-wise it's another component. Suggest we make it lazy and only load if user hits the empty state or clicks "Start quickstart".
Kai: Accessibility points: Ensure trap focus inside modal while open; provide `aria-describedby` for the checklist; use role="dialog" and set `aria-modal=true`. On the modal reveal, announce: "Welcome to Redwood! We'll help you set up in 3 steps." Use `prefers-reduced-motion` to avoid animation for motion-sensitive users.
BotAnne: Automated a11y check (alpha): color contrast warning on step badge (1 low contrast), missing focus visible on the close icon. Also flagged no skip-link present in the modal footer.
Devon: Copy cleanup: Heading "Get started in minutes" -> shorten to "Get started". Step 1 button label: "Create API key" -> "Generate API key". Add microcopy under the key field: "You can rotate this key later in Settings." Also suggest sample project names be action-oriented e.g., "Node quickstart" -> "Try: Node quickstart".
Nina: Good notes. For the modal variant, what is the desired fallback if JS fails? Should we show a server-rendered minimal banner with a link to docs? I don't want users stuck.
Ravi: Yes, fallback banner with progressive enhancement. Also we should persist a cookie (or backend flag) to avoid showing modal repeatedly for dismissed users.
Olivia: Analytics idea: track which onboarding path users take (modal guided vs hero/rail explore) and conversion to first API call. Add event names: `onboard_modal_open`, `onboard_modal_complete`, `sample_project_clone`.
Kai: More a11y: ensure step progress indicator is textual for screen readers (e.g., "Step 1 of 3: Generate API key"). Don't rely solely on color. Test with VoiceOver and NVDA.
Devon: Implementation note: modal state machine should be resilient to navigation away/back. Save progress in localStorage; include TTL of 24 hours. Also ensure that keyboard users can skip to main content (skip link) even when modal isn't needed.
BotAnne: Quick perf sniff: lazy-loading modal reduces initial JS by ~28KB (gzipped) if we defer animation libs. Good to defer.
Nina: OK action list: 1) Prototype modal lazy-load + aria attributes (Kai + Devon). 2) Copy pass (Devon). 3) Add analytics events (Olivia). 4) Add fallback SSR banner (Ravi). 5) a11y manual + axe checks (Kai). Target: have prototype on staging by Tuesday EOD.
Ravi: I'll file tickets with acceptance criteria: accessibility checklist, analytics hooks, SSR banner markup.
Kai: I'll also make a short test plan for QA: keyboard flow, screen reader narration, zoom 200%, contrast, reduced-motion.
Nina: Thanks. If anyone wants to pair on the modal keyboard trap edge cases, ping me. I'll schedule a 30-min pairing on Monday 3pm if needed.
